page_title: Lantern VPN: Nonprofit VPN for fast, private, unrestricted internet access

sources.entry: Lantern - Free application that delivers fast, reliable and secure access to the open internet. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/getlantern/lantern)

summary.name: Lantern
summary.one_liner: Lantern is a nonprofit, open-source VPN that routes blocked sites and apps through its network to get around censorship.
use_cases: Accessing blocked websites and apps in censored regions
Keeping private browsing protected on untrusted networks
Running a personal VPN on your own cloud server
Blocking ads and trackers while browsing
Staying online during protests or internet shutdowns
summary.what_it_does: Lantern sends blocked sites and apps through its network by default and lets all other traffic connect directly, using region-specific smart routing rules. A Full Tunnel mode is available to route everything through the VPN. Its optional Private Server mode lets users run Lantern on their own hardware or cloud account, paying only their own server costs. When one connection method is blocked, Lantern says it switches to another automatically, using multiple protocols. The page also describes built-in ad and tracker blocking and a no-logs policy.
notable: Open source and run by a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Brave New Software Project, Inc.
Smart Routing sends only blocked traffic through the VPN, keeping other sites fast
Optional Private Server mode for self-hosting on your own infrastructure
Automatically switches protocols when one is blocked
caveats: Page says Free to start, and Pro funds open access in censored regions, so some features may require a paid Pro tier; details are not on this page
Private Server mode requires paying your own server costs
Platform list not stated on this page; the awesome-mac listing suggests macOS but this page does not confirm it
